summary.name: Pixel RPG Quest Explainer. An authored Motion Graphic in Motion Design and Cinematography: a technical or educational explainer staged as a game run, where game-progression UI structures the explanation; narrower than Pixel Art (style-057), which covers rendering only.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: a persistent HUD with hearts, a collectible counter that only ever rises (tying its steps to explained concepts is an authored option) and a runtime bar; quest-map chapter cards with cleared and uncleared path segments under a STAGE N plate; a cumulative skill inventory with visible empty slots; pixel dialogue plates with accent end caps; an original pixel guide; dark-grid and cream-paper surfaces with corner brackets, all on one logical pixel grid.
summary.decisionGuidance: Identity: a technical explainer told as a pixel game run, with a persistent HUD, quest-map chapters, a filling skill inventory and dialogue plates. Advantages: progress is visible and earned, which helps long, multi-concept lessons feel structured and motivating for general or developer audiences. Disadvantages: needs a real ordered concept list and tends toward a playful tone; dense diagrams must be redrawn in pixel blocks. Combination fit: stands alone; Pixel Art can tighten sprite work and data storytelling can discipline dense diagrams. Visual constraints: one logical pixel grid, flat limited palette with fixed accent roles, text on solid plates, original characters and icons, HUD values that reflect the story.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: technical and educational explainers, onboarding courses and multi-chapter tutorials. Inferred: product walkthroughs or recap videos that benefit from a sense of progress. Not suited to photoreal, luxury or solemn briefs, or to single-idea clips with nothing to progress. Audience is unspecified.
summary.limitations: HUD values must reflect the real concept and chapter structure and only rise; never decorate with meaningless counters. Do not copy existing game sprites, HUDs, mascots or maps or any source branding. Keep text on solid plates, avoid gradients and anti-aliased glows, and keep unlock flashes brief.
summary.palette: Scene-dependent suggestion: dark grid #1C1F2E, plate ink #11121B, cream text #F4EEDC, cream paper #F2EAD3, highlight orange #F28A2E for keywords and cleared progress, coin yellow #F7C948, heart red #E5484D, success green #5DC26A, item teal #3DB3A6 and muted grey #8D90A6. Roles stay fixed; orange is not a text colour on cream paper.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: stepped whole-pixel motion; inventory slots unlock in one step on their narration cue and map cards arrive already cleared, while any authored counter step lands with the concept it marks; diagrams build nodes before connectors; captions type into pre-sized plates; chapter changes are hard cuts or a short pixel wipe; the guide reacts with small hops. Optional references: Data Build, Terminal Typing, Step-Tick Slot Refill and Elastic Arrival.
summary.audio: Optional light chiptune or lo-fi bed under narration, soft UI blips for unlocks, silence during dense reading. Governed by project audio settings; the catalog preview is silent.
summary.assetRequirements: Topic, ordered concepts, chapters and copy come from the project. Everything can be code-drawn on a pixel grid with bitmap or local monospace lettering; an original guide needs a recorded sprite sheet. Duration, aspect ratio and frame rate are unspecified unless supplied.
summary.combinations: Usually used alone. Pixel Art (style-057) for stricter sprite and palette-cycling scenes; Scientific Visualization / Data Storytelling (style-097) for dense diagram discipline.
summary.productionApproach: Derive all progress values from an ordered concept list; draw SVG or Canvas 2D on one logical grid with crisp edges and bitmap glyphs; keep HUD and captions on a fixed top layer; GSAP drives one paused timeline through a pure time-state function. Composition and export follow the project renderer.
